name: On-chain mempool-congestion demand momentum — ride BTC when the chain is busy
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM (orthogonal to every existing spec — no on-chain feature is used anywhere in the inbox): the Bitcoin mempool size (bytes of unconfirmed transactions waiting for block space) is a real-time, on-chain measure of DEMAND for settlement that users are paying fees to win. Unlike the secularly-trending hashrate/address/tx-count levels, mempool size is mean-reverting (congestion spikes when usage surges, then clears as blocks confirm — ~100k to ~5M bytes, mean ~810k), so a level threshold on it is economically meaningful and stationary rather than the trending-level always-true trap. The thesis: sustained congestion reflects an organic on-chain demand impulse (more economic actors competing for block space) that tends to coincide with or slightly lead price strength — a fundamental, NON-price, NON-sentiment confirmation of a move. Entry: btc_mempool_size above a fitted congestion floor (real on-chain demand) AND price in an uptrend (the congestion confirms the trend, doesn't predict it cold). Exit: mempool crosses DOWN through a clearing threshold (demand impulse fading) or stop/TP/time. Disconfirmer 1: if the unconditional trend long matches the deflated Sharpe, the on-chain gate adds nothing. Disconfirmer 2: mempool congestion can spike on fee-market dislocations unrelated to demand (ordinals/inscriptions waves) — if the edge is concentrated in those windows it is an artifact, not a demand read. Disconfirmer 3 (data depth + applicability): only ~84 daily points and BTC-only (market-wide metric applied to a BTC-led universe) — low-confidence, paper-only until the series deepens. Disconfirmer 4 (cost): must beat buy-and-hold deflated Sharpe net of ~20bps. tier1 on-chain feature.
catalyst: elevated BTC mempool congestion — an on-chain demand impulse confirming a trend
